assumptions: A source node is 0x30 bytes. The routine reads only its +0x00 dword, its +0x10 next pointer, its +0x18 child-list head, and its +0x20..+0x2f tail bytes; it never reads the source +0x08 field, and it never reads or copies the +0x04..+0x07 bytes, which stay uninitialized in each fresh copy.

The routine assumes a non-null source head: its first instructions dereference the source node, and the only observed caller guards a null head before calling. The model raises for a null head instead of modelling a call the binary never makes.

Allocator failure is modelled only once a head copy exists: the landing pad tears down the partial head copy held in r12, and each nested copy invocation tears down its own partial head first, innermost first, before the exception reaches the outer invocation.
A source cycle, a missing node, or a missing field is not silently modelled: the model raises ValueError. The binary would loop or fault on such input; no such input is claimed as a valid case.

callees.contract: operator new with size 0x30 for every copy node, in allocation order: head copy, then its child list, then its siblings in order
operator delete with (node, 0x30) for every node of a partial copy, in the post-order of the teardown routine, when an exception reaches the landing pad
callees.target: 0x5d4c8d0 (node #115 list-tree teardown; open PR #2386 pins its semantics)

callees.contract: exception handling on the landing pads: begin_catch, then teardown and rethrow; end_catch then Unwind_Resume on the second pad

census.note: The three direct calls are the two self-recursive calls at 0x5d4caef (head child list) and 0x5d4cb47 (sibling child list), and the external call at 0x5d80ee3 in the large function; there are no tail jumps, no stored qwords, and no RELATIVE addends.

distinct_from: Open PR #2386 (recursive list-tree teardown 0x5d4c8d0): that routine destroys a list-tree; this routine builds one, and its landing pad calls the teardown. The windows are adjacent but disjoint, and no claim here re-states #2386's semantics.
Open PR #2384 (visited-element teardown 0x5d516f0) and #2383 (element-visit-and-reset 0x5f6eac0): callers of the teardown, not of this routine; no address overlap.
No open PR title or code search hit for 0x5d4caa0.

fields.rule: copied verbatim from the source node to the copy node
never read from the source and never written in the copy; stays uninitialized in the fresh allocation
head copy: the routine's incoming rsi verbatim; sibling copy: the previous copy; child-list head copy: the copy of the parent node. The source node's own +0x08 is never read.
set to 0 at allocation, then set to each following sibling copy as the walk advances; the walk follows the source +0x10 chain in order
set to 0 at allocation, then set to the recursive copy of the source node's +0x18 list, or left 0 when that list is null
copied verbatim as 16 bytes from the source node to the copy node

not_claimed: Caller semantics beyond the 0x5d80ee3 site's argument setup, guard, and post-call walks; in particular what the rbx/rbp objects or their +0x20b0/+0x20c8/+0x20d0/+0x20d8/+0x20e0/+0x20e8 fields denote.
Which try region each landing pad guards; the pads are stated literally as trailing blocks, not mapped to regions.
Any meaning for the node fields beyond the copy rules, and any behavior for a null source head, which the routine never handles because its caller guards it.
The +0x04..+0x07 contents of any copy, which the routine never reads or writes.

routine.returns: the head copy address, in rax
routine.takes: source head in rdi, link value in rsi

site.guard: the call is skipped entirely when the qword at [rbp+0x20d0] is zero
site.post_call: the caller walks the copy's +0x10 chain to its last node and stores it at [rbx+0x20d8], walks the copy's +0x18 chain from the head to its last node and stores it at [rbx+0x20e0], stores the head copy at [rbx+0x20d0], and stores the qword at [rbp+0x20e8] at [rbx+0x20e8]
site.pre_call: the caller stores 0 at [rbx+0x20d0] and [rbx+0x20e8], stores rbx+0x20c8 at [rbx+0x20d8] and [rbx+0x20e0], stores 0 as a dword at [rbx+0x20c8], and stores r13 at [rbx+0x20b0]
